verdicts.rewritten_summary: Association for Legal Intervention (13 Mar 2024): a Polish regional court placed a transgender woman (Vietnamese citizen, on hormone therapy since 2018) in a guarded centre for male foreigners; Border Guard refused to move/release her despite her identifying as a woman and warning that stopping medication would harm her. After an intervention by the legal-aid organisation citing Polish law, court rulings and international standards, the Border Guard Commander released her because continued detention there posed a serious health risk. Useful to this record: in Poland, detained foreign trans women face placement in male-only facilities until formally challenged, and release can depend on legal intervention.

TGEU, 16 Jul 2024: on 11 July 2024 the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) found Polish prison authorities violated Article 8 (right to private and family life) of the ECHR by denying a trans woman access to hormone replacement therapy while imprisoned, despite her having been prescribed hormones for almost two years; the Court awarded EUR 8,000 damages. Useful to this record: a trans visitor who is detained in Poland has a Europe-wide human-rights remedy against denial of HRT, though enforcement required litigation.

Sahara Reporters, 19 Aug 2026: the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) travel advice for Nigeria warns LGBT+ travellers of attacks, a 14-year jail term under the 2014 Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act, and possible death-penalty risks in northern states under Sharia criminal law. Useful to this record: UK's official advisory states that LGBT+ travellers to Nigeria face arrest, violence, blackmail and intimidation, with 14-year imprisonment for same-sex unions and sharia death-penalty risk in some northern states — the national frame that applies in full in this southern state.

BBC News, 9 Aug 2024: Nigerian police investigated the death of 33-year-old transgender TikToker 'Abuja Area Mama', whose beaten body was found along a highway in the federal capital Abuja. She had posted about being transgender and working as a sex worker, and had expressed fears for her life in the previous year. Useful to this record: nationally reported evidence (Aug 2024) that transgender people in Nigeria face lethal violence, with a police statement that 'preliminary investigations revealed that the individual was a man fully dressed in female clothing' — documenting official framing as well as the killing; applies nationally, no state-specific divergence recorded.
